title: RAW NATIVE-INFORMED: homologous internal run lengths distinguish copying a chosen spelling from rebuilding two similar parts
summary: Exploratory structural hypothesis grounded in the retained B/By/Bdy/BBdy families, exact word profiles, stable e/i lengths and local spelling-choice limits. Under one deliberately narrow echo-family contract, a writer first chooses a complete written body, copies it literally and writes dy once outside the copies. Homologous strictly internal e/i runs must then have equal lengths. Candidate selection uses identical run-collapsed half skeletons rather than prior literal equality, so mismatches remain visible. Same skeletons do not prove same source identity or copying. No meaning, test result, general parser or native fit is asserted.

design.mechanism: Plan a complete body spelling U once, including its e/i multiplicities, then duplicate that written plan as UU and append the literal family tail dy once. Repetition might have some unknown lexical/grammatical role, but no role value is assigned. The rival order rebuilds two parts separately or uses a learned whole form; no distribution for that rival is invented.
design.unit: One complete written group in a prospectively fixed dy-ending echo-family subset; the working units and boundaries remain transcription premises, not a recovered alphabet.
design.contrast: Within-token fidelity of homologous internal run lengths, not frequency excess of identical halves, generic nearby copying, equality of external contexts, a new geometric run law, or a whole-word language decoder.
design.prediction: If every eligible form in the declared subset is generated by copying one already fully chosen spelling, each pair of corresponding internal e/i runs has exactly equal length. Unequal lengths reject only that universal subset/renderer contract; they do not reject copying elsewhere, independent allography after copying, two distinct source bodies or a learned atomic whole.

native_motivation.productive_parts_with_whole_limits: The approved composition/forms topics retain directed reusable structure and whole-form residuals, without establishing morphemes, a unique parser or native meanings. This hypothesis leaves whole-form memory and ambiguity available as rivals, not as invisible exceptions within the tested copy contract.

native_motivation.position_limit: ololdy's two occurrences per reading are line-internal on two leaves; chchdy's single occurrence is line-final. They do not supply a universal line-final closure rule. Their spelling is retained independently of their different positions.
native_motivation.run_constraint: GDT1328rejects independent memoryless elongation even within exact page/collapsed-whole/slot cells. Stable selected spellings could contribute to this regularity, but1328does not show that run differences are meaningless or that a two-length cap is valid. The current copy rule introduces no new run-length distribution or cap.
native_motivation.local_choice_limit: GDT1333finds no retained word+site predictive increment after immediately flanking expanded primitives, while reporting positive descriptive local gains. This makes a locally rebuilt spelling a reasonable rival, not a confirmed cause or permission to identify bench forms. Its failed conjunction, direction nonselection and remaining alternatives stay unchanged.

one_prospective_discriminator.index_only: For a complete dy-final working-unit string, remove exactly that terminal d,y for this family question only. Let C collapse each maximal e-run to one e and each maximal i-run to one i, leaving every other working unit unchanged. C is only an exploratory index; it is not a licensed transcription correction or content decoder.
one_prospective_discriminator.nomination: Require the collapsed remainder to be exactly TT for a nonempty skeleton T. Its half boundary is fixed by the collapsed sequence, not optimized for run agreement. Retain only comparisons having at least one e/i position strictly inside T, away from both ends. Each such position corresponds to one maximal run in each original half.
one_prospective_discriminator.seams: If identical e/i families would coalesce across a proposed half seam, the simple TTindex does not identify that seam and the case is outside this initial comparison. Do not invent a split inside one uninterrupted run. Border runs are not the primary comparison; only strictly internal corresponding runs are compared.
one_prospective_discriminator.comparison: Compare the two lengths at every nominated internal e/i position. Candidate eligibility must NOT require equality of the original literal halves or of their lengths. Mismatches must remain rather than being reclassified as a different convenient base.
one_prospective_discriminator.no_extra_normalization: Keep e and i distinct. Do not expand ckh/cth/cph/cfh under BH/HB, change readers' spaces, merge annotations, alter dy, or pool different base skeletons/pages to create a favorable result. No such rule is supplied by1333.
one_prospective_discriminator.interpretation: For an eligible index position j, the necessary literal-copy consequence is length(firstcopy,j)=length(secondcopy,j). This is an exact descriptive contrast, not a probability model, a p-value or an estimate of the amount of copying in the manuscript.

critical_identity_and_reader_limit: Equal collapsed halves do NOT independently show that they are the same source base or that this complete word was produced by copy. A mismatch therefore refutes only an explicit claim applying the literal-copy-after-spelling rule to ALLeligible forms of a nominated subset.

GDT1200already gives the actual ololdy ambiguity: ol+ol+dy and olol+dy have available whole-form support, with olol14/14/14and ololy1/1/1. This cannot be solved by silently deleting olol from a dictionary or declaring its meaning compositional.

The proposed writer can mechanically duplicate U, but a semantic reader still needs a justified choice between copy(U), a compound of different bodies, and atomicUU. No invented meaning or message-equivalence claim supplies that choice here. The RAW is not a complete content-preserving decoder.

Equality of the two runs would be compatible with literal copying, but also with independently written equal parts or a fixed whole-form spelling. It is not proof of a mental copying event, native reduplication or identical meanings.

A context-dependent change after copying would be outside the narrow renderer. It must not be added automatically to explain a counterexample. Conversely the failure of that narrow renderer would not disprove all context-sensitive handwriting.
known_countercases_and_capacity_limits: The positive closed al/ch/olrepeats motivating1200contain no strictly internal e/i runs. They motivate the construction problem but provide no capacity for THISrun-fidelity comparison. No eligible new contrast or positive count has been found in this producer block.
daldaldyis a closed ZLform but split in the other readings; alaldyhas an RFannotation/boundary difference. These must not be upgraded to three-reader closed repetitions.

dydydyexists butdyydoes not complete the same family; dardardyis a three-word case in IT/RF, and one chol/choldy seam is uncertain. None permits a universal recursive-repeat parser or a free regrouping of words.
The forms topic retains qokdy/okdy, so d after k does not require e. Additional eeforms also exist. No fixed e-count or automatic e/dexclusion is inserted into this hypothesis.
The chchdyprofile has other nonidentical close forms. Edit distance does not make their bodies aliases or prove a copied part; those forms are not silently normalized into the echo family.

Sparse genuine opportunities may leave this question uninformative. The declared response is to retain that limitation, not weaken previous thresholds, extend windows or search other tails until a contrast appears.
